title: Units and Measurement
description: We measure time in seconds, minutes, hours, and days. We measure distance in centimetres, metres, and kilometres. Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

exercises.question: Which unit do we use to measure a SHORT time (like a heartbeat)?
exercises.exp: Seconds are very short units of time. Your heart beats about once per second!

exercises.question: Which unit is best for measuring the length of your pencil?
exercises.exp: A pencil is about 19 centimetres long — centimetres work perfectly for small objects.

exercises.question: Which unit is best for measuring the DISTANCE from Toronto to Ottawa?
exercises.exp: Long distances like city-to-city are measured in kilometres. Toronto to Ottawa is about 450 km!

exercises.question: How many minutes are in 1 HOUR?
exercises.exp: There are 60 minutes in one hour. And 60 seconds in one minute!

exercises.question: How many days are in 1 WEEK?
exercises.exp: There are 7 days in a week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

exercises.question: What abbreviation is used for CENTIMETRES?
exercises.exp: cm is the abbreviation for centimetre. 100 cm = 1 metre.

exercises.question: What abbreviation is used for KILOGRAMS?
exercises.exp: kg is the abbreviation for kilogram. A kilogram = 1000 grams.

exercises.question: Which is heavier — 1 kilogram or 500 grams?
exercises.exp: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams. So 1 kg is twice as heavy as 500 g!

exercises.question: A swimming pool holds thousands of litres of water. What are litres used to measure?
exercises.exp: Litres (L) measure volume — how much liquid fits in a space. Millilitres (mL) are smaller units.

exercises.question: What abbreviation stands for MILLILITRES?
exercises.exp: mL stands for millilitres. 1000 mL = 1 litre. A teaspoon holds about 5 mL.

exercises.question: A baby kitten weighs 100 grams. A bag of flour weighs 1 kilogram. Which is heavier?
exercises.exp: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams. The flour bag is 10 times heavier than the kitten!

exercises.question: Which unit would you use to measure the height of a door?
exercises.exp: A door is about 2 metres tall — metres are perfect for measuring heights of rooms and doors.

exercises.question: How many centimetres are in 1 METRE?
exercises.exp: There are 100 centimetres in 1 metre. Centi means one hundredth — so a centimetre is 1/100 of a metre!

exercises.question: How many grams are in 1 KILOGRAM?
exercises.exp: Kilo means one thousand — so 1 kilogram = 1000 grams. A large water bottle weighs about 1 kilogram!

exercises.question: How many millilitres are in 1 LITRE?
exercises.exp: There are 1000 millilitres (mL) in 1 litre (L). A standard water bottle usually holds 500 mL — half a litre.

exercises.question: Which unit is the SMALLEST unit of time listed here?
exercises.exp: Seconds are the smallest — 60 seconds make a minute, 60 minutes make an hour, 24 hours make a day!

exercises.question: How many hours are in 1 DAY?
exercises.exp: There are 24 hours in one day — the time it takes Earth to rotate once on its axis!

exercises.question: What abbreviation is used for METRES?
exercises.exp: m is the abbreviation for metre. It is the base unit of length in the metric system.

exercises.question: What abbreviation is used for KILOMETRES?
exercises.exp: km stands for kilometre. 1 km = 1000 metres. Kilo always means 1000!

exercises.question: What abbreviation is used for GRAMS?
exercises.exp: g is the abbreviation for grams. A small grape weighs about 5 grams.

exercises.question: What abbreviation is used for LITRES?
exercises.exp: L is the abbreviation for litre. A large carton of milk holds about 2 L (two litres).

exercises.question: Which is LONGER — 1 metre or 50 centimetres?
choices: it depends on what you are measuring
exercises.exp: 1 metre = 100 centimetres. So 1 metre is twice as long as 50 centimetres!

exercises.question: A medicine dropper holds about 1 mL. How many droppers would fill a 1-litre bottle?
exercises.exp: 1 litre = 1000 mL — so you would need 1000 medicine droppers to fill a 1-litre bottle!

exercises.question: How many weeks are in 1 YEAR?
exercises.exp: There are 52 weeks in a year. And 365 days (or 366 in a leap year)!

exercises.question: Which unit would best measure the width of your FINGERNAIL?
exercises.exp: A fingernail is about 10 mm wide — millimetres are perfect for very tiny measurements!

exercises.question: How many months are in 1 YEAR?
exercises.exp: There are 12 months in a year: January through December.

exercises.question: A car trip takes 2 hours and 30 minutes. How many minutes is that in total?
exercises.exp: 2 hours = 120 minutes, plus 30 minutes = 150 minutes total. There are 60 minutes in each hour!

exercises.question: You have 2500 mL of juice. How many LITRES is that?
exercises.exp: 1000 mL = 1 L. So 2500 mL ÷ 1000 = 2.5 litres. You can pour 2 full litre jugs and have half a litre left!

exercises.question: Which weighs MORE — a 2-kilogram bag of rice or 1500 grams of flour?
exercises.exp: 2 kg = 2000 grams. 2000 g is heavier than 1500 g — the rice bag wins by 500 grams!

exercises.question: A swimming race takes 58 seconds. Is that MORE or LESS than 1 minute?
exercises.exp: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 58 seconds is just 2 seconds less than 1 minute — a very fast swim!

exercises.question: What do we call the standard system of units used in science that includes metres, kilograms, and litres?
exercises.exp: The Metric system (SI) is the standard in science. It uses metres for distance, kilograms for mass, and litres for volume!

exercises.question: You walk 3 kilometres to school every day. How many METRES do you walk?
exercises.exp: 1 km = 1000 m. So 3 km = 3 × 1000 = 3000 metres. That is a good walk — about 30–40 minutes!

exercises.question: Which tool measures LENGTH?
exercises.exp: A ruler measures length in centimetres and millimetres. A measuring tape works for longer distances in metres!

exercises.question: Which tool measures TEMPERATURE?
exercises.exp: A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F). Digital and mercury thermometers are common!

exercises.question: Which tool measures the VOLUME of a liquid most accurately?
exercises.exp: A measuring cylinder has graduated markings to measure liquid volume in millilitres (mL) accurately. Read the bottom of the meniscus!

exercises.question: Which tool measures MASS?
choices: a balance scale or digital scale
exercises.exp: A balance scale compares mass to known weights. A digital scale shows mass in grams or kilograms — both measure mass!

exercises.question: 1 centimetre (cm) equals how many millimetres (mm)?
exercises.exp: 1 cm = 10 mm. The prefix 'centi' means 100th, and 'milli' means 1000th. So 1 cm = 10 mm!

exercises.question: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
exercises.exp: 1 kilogram (kg) = 1000 grams (g). The prefix 'kilo' always means 1000 in the metric system!

exercises.question: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
exercises.exp: 1 litre (L) = 1000 millilitres (mL). A standard water bottle is 500 mL — half a litre!

exercises.question: A book has a mass of 450 grams. Another book has a mass of 0.45 kg. Which is HEAVIER?
choices: they are the same mass — 450 g = 0.45 kg
exercises.exp: 0.45 kg = 450 g — they are identical masses! Converting: 0.45 × 1000 = 450 g.

exercises.question: A fever is when your temperature is ABOVE 37°C (normal body temperature). Which reading indicates a fever?
exercises.exp: Normal body temperature is about 37°C. A temperature of 38.5°C is above normal — that indicates a fever!

exercises.question: Water FREEZES at ___ °C and BOILS at ___ °C.
exercises.exp: Water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C (Celsius). The Fahrenheit equivalents are 32°F and 212°F — but science uses Celsius!

exercises.question: You have a 250 mL cup and a 1 L bottle. How many full cups fit in the bottle?
exercises.exp: 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 ÷ 250 = 4. You can fill the cup exactly 4 times from the bottle!

exercises.question: Which is the LIGHTEST?
exercises.exp: 500 g < 1000 g (1 kg) < 1500 g < 2000 g (2 kg). So 500 g is the lightest! Convert everything to grams to compare.

exercises.question: A recipe needs 2.5 kg of flour. You have a bag with 2500 g. Do you have enough?
choices: no — 2500 g is more than 2.5 kg
no — 2500 g is less than 2.5 kg
you cannot compare grams and kilograms
exercises.exp: 2.5 kg = 2.5 × 1000 = 2500 g. You have exactly the right amount!

exercises.question: You pour 350 mL of water into a jug that already has 750 mL. How much water is in the jug now?
exercises.exp: 750 + 350 = 1100 mL. That is 1.1 litres (just over 1 L) in the jug!

exercises.question: A pencil is 18 cm long. A pen is 145 mm long. Which is LONGER?
exercises.exp: Convert the pencil: 18 cm = 180 mm. 180 mm > 145 mm — the pencil is longer!

exercises.question: Which METRIC unit would you use to measure the distance between two cities?
exercises.exp: Kilometres are perfect for long distances — cities are usually tens or hundreds of km apart. 1 km = 1000 m.

exercises.question: Which metric unit is BEST for measuring the mass of a grain of rice?
exercises.exp: A grain of rice weighs about 25 mg (milligrams)! For tiny masses, milligrams are the right unit. 1 g = 1000 mg.

exercises.question: What does the prefix 'MILLI-' mean in the metric system?
exercises.exp: Milli- means one thousandth. So 1 millimetre = 1/1000 of a metre, and 1 millilitre = 1/1000 of a litre!

exercises.question: Scientists use the METRIC system because ___.
choices: it is the oldest system of measurement
it is based on powers of 10, making conversions simple — just multiply or divide by 10, 100, or 1000
it uses harder units to learn
only scientists are allowed to use it
exercises.exp: The metric system's base-10 design makes conversions easy — no awkward fractions like 12 inches to a foot. Just move the decimal!

exercises.question: A swimming pool holds 2,500,000 litres of water. In kilolitres (1 kL = 1000 L), this is ___.
exercises.exp: 2,500,000 L ÷ 1000 = 2500 kL. The prefix kilo- means 1000, so divide by 1000 to convert litres to kilolitres!
